title: Introduce opaque credential providers and stream-signal hooks; Go SDK ergonomics parity
author: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: bring the Go SDK closer to parity with Python/TypeScript on credential ergonomics and streaming control hooks. Customers reported friction when swapping credential providers and when trying to emit custom stream-level signals (heartbeat/backpressure) from Go. This PR introduces an OpaqueCredentialProvider interface to allow pluggable credential lifecycles and a lightweight StreamSignalHook API to surface heartbeat and backpressure hints to the runtime.

What this PR does (high level):
- Add OpaqueCredentialProvider interface + default implementations (Static, RotatingWindow, DelegatingChain).
- Introduce StreamSignalHook and two built-in hooks: HeartbeatHint and BackpressureHint. Hooks are opt-in on stream creation.
- Provide an adapter for legacy credentials so existing users do not need immediate migration.
- Improve error ergonomics on auth failures: typed errors and helper methods to introspect transient vs terminal auth errors.
- Small surface parity changes: align method names with py/ts SDKs (StreamHandle -> Stream), add WithSignalHooks opts, and bump go module to v1.5.4.
- Tests: unit tests for provider rotation, integration test that exercises hook emission while streaming tokens, and additional fuzzing for credential adapters.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-1024)
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Backwards-compatible adapter for legacy credentials
- [x] Docs updated (README and migration note)
- [x] Version bump and changelog entry

Notes on compatibility: migration is opt-in. The legacy credential API remains functional via CredentialAdapter; a deprecation notice was added to the README and will be removed in two minor versions. The StreamSignalHook is additive and cannot break existing streams but can change scheduling behavior when hooks emit BackpressureHint frequently.

Performance/observability: emitting BackpressureHint toggles an internal tracing tag and exposes a metric sdk.stream.backpressure_hints_emitted which is toggled in the runtime; a follow-up PR will wire this to the console dashboards.
